conventions.convention: Spectra are taken in the stated ambient algebra, and for a nonunital Banach algebra the spectrum of an element is by convention computed in the named unitization C⊕A; containment of invertible groups makes the spectrum in a subalgebra larger, and spectra may strictly shrink in a larger algebra.
Resolvent convention R(z,a) = (z1−a)^{−1}; with this order the resolvent identity reads R(z,a)−R(w,a) = (w−z)R(z,a)R(w,a) and the derivative of the resolvent is −R(z,a)^2.

A unital Banach algebra is nonzero, complex, with associative bilinear multiplication, a submultiplicative norm under which it is complete, and a two-sided unit 1 with ‖1‖=1; invertibility always means two-sided invertibility.

Characters are nonzero multiplicative linear maps; continuity and unitality are not part of the definition but are theorems for a nonzero unital Banach algebra, where every character is unital, has χ(a) in σ_A(a) and satisfies |χ(a)| ≤ ‖a‖ with ‖χ‖=1.

C*-algebras may be zero and need not be unital; positivity means a=b*b; approximate units are nets over a nonempty directed set of positive contractions; no unitary notion is claimed in a genuinely nonunital algebra.

Degenerate conventions are fixed explicitly: C(∅)={0} with Δ({0})=∅, C_0(∅)={0}, the one-element Boolean algebra has empty Stone space with Clop(∅) trivial, and the rank-zero bundle has e(0_B)=1, c(0_B)=1, w(0_B)=1, p_0(E)=1.
Reduced generalized (co)homology theories impose no dimension axiom; coefficient groups are h^q(*) = h̃^q(S^0) = h^q(pt); the wedge axiom is a product in cohomology and a direct sum in homology.
Skeletal filtration conventions X^p=∅ for p<0 and X^p=X for p≥dim X; the AHSS theorems and their convergence are stated for finite CW complexes only, and no infinite-CW convergence is asserted.

AHSS indexing: cohomologically E_1^{p,q}=h^{p+q}(X^p,X^{p−1}) with d_r of bidegree (r,1−r); homologically E^1_{p,q}=h_{p+q}(X^p,X^{p−1}) with d^r of bidegree (−r,r−1); the first page is called E_1 (never E_0).

Chern-class normalization: c_1(L)=e(L_R) with the complex orientation (v_1,iv_1,…) positive, and x=e(γ_R) is the projective-bundle generator; on CP^1 the clutching/Hopf generator u is the negative of c_1(γ*) and hence of the projective-pair generator, each example stating which orientation of the sphere it uses.

Orientation signs: for an oriented real rank-2n bundle V the complex orientation of (V_C)_R differs from the product orientation by (−1)^n, so e((V_C)_R)=(−1)^n e(V)^2; Pontryagin classes are p_i(E)=(−1)^i c_{2i}(E_C), with p_i=0 whenever 2i>rank_R E.
Euler class convention e(ξ)=s*j*(u_ξ) with the relative-to-absolute map included; e(0_B)=1; over F_2 every real bundle is canonically oriented; reversing an integral orientation negates e.

Admissible bases are paracompact Hausdorff spaces of CW type, with numerable finite-rank bundles; characteristic classes are only evaluated over bases that are both admissible and in the classification scope, and CW complexes qualify for both.

Chern character: ch_k=(1/k!)N_k(c_1,…,c_n) with N_k the Newton polynomial for the power sum, so coefficients lie in Q; the graded character is defined by suspension and normalized on the Bott class before any graded statement, and the calculus of the K-AHSS comparison uses h^j(X)=⊕_kH^{j+2k}(X;Q).

load_bearing.statement: A unital complex Banach algebra is a nonzero complex vector space with associative bilinear multiplication, a submultiplicative norm under which it is a Banach space, and a unit 1 with ‖1‖=1.
σ_A(a) = {z ∈ C : z1−a ∉ A^×}, ρ_A(a)=C∖σ_A(a) and R(z,a)=(z1−a)^{−1}, with the ambient algebra part of the data and spectra possibly shrinking in a larger algebra.

For a finite CW complex X and reduced generalized cohomology theory h̃ there is a cohomological spectral sequence with E_1^{p,q}=h^{p+q}(X^p,X^{p−1}), E_2^{p,q}≅H^p(X;h^q(*)), d_r:E_r^{p,q}→E_r^{p+r,q−r+1}, stable page E_∞^{p,q}≅F^p h^{p+q}(X)/F^{p+1}h^{p+q}(X), natural in X for cellular maps and in the theory for morphisms.

A reduced generalized cohomology theory on based CW complexes is contravariant functors h̃^n with natural suspension isomorphisms σ:h̃^n(X)→h̃^{n+1}(ΣX) and natural connecting maps δ_f:h̃^n(X)→h̃^{n+1}(C_f) satisfying (H) homotopy invariance, (E) exactness of the cofiber sequence and (W) the wedge axiom; no dimension axiom is imposed.

Reduced generalized cohomology theories on based CW complexes and CW-pair cohomology theories satisfying (H), (LES), (Ex) and (Add) determine one another through h^n(X,A)=h̃^n(C_i) and h̃^n(Y)=h^n(Y,*), with h^n(X,A)≅h̃^n(X/A) for A≠∅, the two constructions canonically inverse and the connecting maps agreeing.

The Chern classes c_i(E) ∈ H^{2i}(B;Z) are the unique coefficients in the monic projective-bundle relation x_E^n − a_1x_E^{n−1} + a_2x_E^{n−2} − ⋯ + (−1)^n a_n = 0, with c_0(E)=1, c_i(E)=0 for i>n, and c_1(L)=e(L_R) in the complex orientation.

For a numerable complex rank-n bundle E over a path-connected CW complex (or CW-type base) B, H^*(P(E);R) is a free H^*(B;R)-module with basis 1,x_R,…,x_R^{n−1} for R=Z and every F_p, and the expansion of x^n is the unique monic relation generating all polynomial relations.

The Stiefel–Whitney classes w_i(E) ∈ H^i(B;F_2) are the unique coefficients of the monic relation x_E^n + c_1x_E^{n−1} + ⋯ + c_n = 0 in H^n(P(E);F_2), with w_0(E)=1, w_i(E)=0 for i>n, and w_1(L)=x_L for a line.

For a nonzero unital complex Banach algebra A, every character χ is unital, satisfies χ(a)∈σ_A(a) and |χ(a)|≤‖a‖, and is therefore bounded linear with ‖χ‖=1 (an argument run on the Neumann series, a theorem of ZF).
For a nonzero unital commutative complex C*-algebra A the Gelfand transform Γ:A→C(Δ(A)) is an isometric unital ∗-isomorphism onto C(Δ(A)), with Γ(a*)=conj(Γ(a)) and ‖Γ(a)‖_∞=‖a‖ for all a.
p_i(E):=(−1)^i c_{2i}(E_C) ∈ H^{4i}(B;Z), with p_0(E)=1 and p_i(E)=0 whenever 2i>rank_R E; the definition requires no orientation and the odd Chern classes of E_C enter no Pontryagin class.

concerns.concern: The statement includes naturality in X for cellular maps and in the theory for morphisms, but the proof only asserts this in step 5.1 ("naturality is inherited from the naturality of the pair long exact sequences and of the exact-couple construction"); the map-of-exact-couples proposition is not in the deps list, and the page proves the naturality statement only in the separate item thm-naturality-and-edge-maps-of-the-ahss. A reader must supply that cross-reference to close the naturality clause as stated.

The (τ,σ)-component of d_1 is asserted to be multiplication by the degree of the composite "attaching map of e^{p+1} followed by collapse onto the σ-sphere" (steps 1.2-2.1), matching the incidence number [e^{p+1}:e^p] exactly; this normalization depends on the library's suspension convention (sphere coordinate first, def-reduced-generalized-cohomology-theory) and on the connecting maps of the pair long exact sequences, and the identification is made by appeal to the cited source diagram rather than recomputed from the local definitions. The claim d_1 = δ (rather than −δ) is the point to check against those conventions.

Step 2.1 concludes that the E_3 source, target and d_3 of the ku- and KU-skeletal AHSSs agree, from an E_1-level coefficient isomorphism plus "naturality for theory morphisms". This presupposes that ku's representing spectrum gives a reduced generalized cohomology theory in the sense of def-reduced-generalized-cohomology-theory (so that the AHSS theorem applies and E_2 computes H^p(X;coefficient ring) in the translated rows); no dependency listed supplies that the spectrum ku (rather than the bundle model of K-theory) satisfies those axioms, and the proof only displays the E_1 coefficient comparison.

The load-bearing inputs are recorded source computations rather than local proofs: H^3(H)≅Z/2 generated by δ_2Sq^2, the nonvanishing δ_2Sq^2≠0 in H^6(H,3), H^6(SU)=0, and the Bott-cofiber boundary k_*f^3=β_2Sq^2f^0 (F5/F6, explicitly "not assertions reproved in this library"). The local proof adds only the Z/2 dichotomy. Since lem-ku-representability... and thm-first-possible-complex-k-ahss-differential... consume this exact normalization, the source-read status is load-bearing for the K-AHSS d_3 formula.
